result.reviewScopeSummary: Initial verification of Story 0 foundation against the story, full Epic 5 tech-design set, and test plan. I inspected the shared artifact/review contracts, review routes and services, Convex package-context persistence, Story 0 fixtures/tests, and the implementor artifact, then ran the requested story and epic gates.

newFindings.title: Shared package-member vocabulary still uses legacy `versionId` instead of the Story 0 `artifactVersionId` field
newFindings.evidence: Story 0 defines package members with `artifactVersionId` as the pinned version identifier (`docs/spec-build/v2/epics/05--artifact-model-and-review-provenance-alignment/stories/00-foundation.md:105-113`). The shipped browser contract still exports `packageMemberSchema.versionId` (`apps/platform/shared/contracts/review-workspace.ts:263-271`), `package-review.service.ts` consumes `member.versionId` throughout (`apps/platform/server/services/review/package-review.service.ts:30-61,118-123`), and the Story 0 implementor artifact explicitly records this as a deferred spec deviation (`.../artifacts/00-foundation/001-implementor.json`).

newFindings.title: Review endpoints still collapse missing-version and missing-member cases into generic or legacy outcomes
newFindings.evidence: Story 0 requires route-level distinction among `REVIEW_TARGET_NOT_FOUND`, `ARTIFACT_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`, `PACKAGE_MEMBER_UNAVAILABLE`, and `PACKAGE_MEMBER_NOT_ALLOWED` (`docs/spec-build/v2/epics/05--artifact-model-and-review-provenance-alignment/stories/00-foundation.md:123-140`). In the implementation, `artifact-review.service.ts` returns `null` when an explicit `versionId` is missing (`apps/platform/server/services/review/artifact-review.service.ts:113-120`), and `routes/review.ts` converts any `null` artifact/package lookup into `404 REVIEW_TARGET_NOT_FOUND` (`apps/platform/server/routes/review.ts:287-301,364-378`). Bounded workspace degradation is also hard-coded to `REVIEW_TARGET_NOT_FOUND` (`apps/platform/server/services/review/review-workspace.service.ts:159-183`), while package-member degradation still emits legacy `REVIEW_MEMBER_UNAVAILABLE` (`apps/platform/server/services/review/package-review.service.ts:19-27,125-132`). The passing server suite locks this behavior in by expecting `200` plus `REVIEW_MEMBER_UNAVAILABLE` for a missing explicit `memberId` (`tests/service/server/package-review-api.test.ts:539-579`).

newFindings.title: The new canonical package-context upsert invariant is not backed by the planned automated proof
newFindings.evidence: Story 0 makes one-current-package-context semantics, duplicate cleanup, and idempotent upsert part of the foundation (`docs/spec-build/v2/epics/05--artifact-model-and-review-provenance-alignment/stories/00-foundation.md:115-121,136-138`). The Convex mutation does implement canonical-row selection, duplicate cleanup, and idempotent early return (`convex/processPackageContexts.ts:110-237`), but the authoritative test inventory assigns that proof to `convex/processPackageContexts.test.ts` (`docs/spec-build/v2/epics/05--artifact-model-and-review-provenance-alignment/test-plan.md:160-161,236-240`) and that file is absent. I also found no reviewed test that exercises `upsertCurrentProcessPackageContext`.

mockOrShimAuditFindings: Server review/package tests rely heavily on `InMemoryPlatformStore`, and that shim still models package members with legacy `versionId` plus `REVIEW_MEMBER_UNAVAILABLE`; the test double currently reinforces the Story 0 vocabulary drift instead of exposing it.
openQuestions: Was the compatibility bridge for legacy `versionId` / `REVIEW_MEMBER_UNAVAILABLE` intentionally accepted for Story 0? The story text and test plan both read as exact aligned vocabulary, not a transitional bridge.
additionalObservations: Both requested gates passed, but the passing suites currently validate the compatibility bridge rather than the exact Story 0 package-member and error-taxonomy contracts.
`guard:no-test-changes` and `test:e2e` are scaffolded skips in this repo, so they did not contribute additional Story 0 behavior coverage.
The implementor artifact already lists the `versionId` and `REVIEW_MEMBER_UNAVAILABLE` bridges as spec deviations, which matches Findings S0-F1 and S0-F2.
